title: Fix the Broken Cron File
description: Two jobs never run: one cron.d line has 7 fields, another uses an invalid */0 step. Repair both.
scenario: Two scheduled jobs on this box have never fired, and syslog shows cron discarding their lines as malformed. /etc/cron.d/nightly-report has a line with SEVEN fields (an extra '*' someone pasted in) and a cleanup line using the nonsense step '*/0'. Repair both lines to the runbook targets: the report job at 03:30 daily and the cleanup job at 05:15 daily, both as root.
symptoms: Neither send-report.sh nor cleanup-temp.sh has ever run
The first active line of /etc/cron.d/nightly-report has 7 fields
The second line uses an invalid '*/0' step value
cron logs warn about malformed lines every time it reloads
mission: Repair /etc/cron.d/nightly-report so its two active lines are `30 3 * * * root /usr/local/bin/send-report.sh` and `15 5 * * * root /usr/local/bin/cleanup-temp.sh`.

hints.title: Eight fields is one too many
hints.content: /etc/cron.d lines have exactly seven: five time fields, the username, then the command. The broken line has EIGHT — an extra '*' shifts everything and cron reads a wrong username.

hints.title: Step values can't be zero
hints.content: `*/0` means 'every 0 minutes' — undefined. Valid steps look like */5, */15, */10. Here the runbook simply wants a fixed time: 15 5 * * *.

hints.title: Rewrite the whole file
hints.content: With only two active lines, the safest fix is rewriting the file cleanly with sudo tee rather than surgical seds.

acceptance_criteria.description: the report job line is exactly '30 3 * * * root /usr/local/bin/send-report.sh'
the cleanup job line is exactly '15 5 * * * root /usr/local/bin/cleanup-temp.sh'
every active line has exactly 7 fields (5 time fields + username + command)
